You can find **olive oil** in a variety of places, depending on your location, budget, and quality preferences. Here are the best places to look:

### **1. Grocery Stores & Supermarkets**
Most large supermarkets carry olive oil in the **cooking oil aisle** or the **international foods section**. Common brands include:
- **Budget-friendly:** Bertolli, Filippo Berio, Pompeian
- **Mid-range:** Colavita, California Olive Ranch, Lucini
- **Premium:** Lucini Premium Select, Cobram Estate, Gaea

**Where to check:**
- **Walmart, Target, Kroger, Safeway, Publix, Whole Foods, Trader Joe’s, Aldi, Lidl**

### **2. Specialty & Gourmet Stores**
For **high-quality, extra virgin olive oil (EVOO)**, check:
- **Whole Foods Market** (has a good selection of organic and imported EVOO)
- **Trader Joe’s** (affordable but decent quality, like their **TJ’s 100% Greek Kalamata Olive Oil**)
- **Eataly** (if you have one nearby, great for Italian imports)
- **Local gourmet shops** (often carry small-batch, artisanal oils)

### **3. Online Retailers (Best for Variety & Bulk)**
If you want **fresh, high-quality, or rare olive oils**, online is the best option:
- **Amazon** (wide selection, but check reviews for authenticity)
  - Top picks: **Brightland, Cobram Estate, Kasandrinos, Lucini**
- **Thrive Market** (organic & specialty oils at a discount)
- **Olive Oil Lovers** ([oliveoillovers.com](https://www.oliveoillovers.com)) – Specializes in premium EVOO
- **Amazon Fresh / Whole Foods Delivery** (for quick delivery)
- **Direct from producers** (e.g., **California Olive Ranch, McEvoy Ranch, Brightland**)

### **4. Farmers Markets & Local Producers**
Many **local farmers markets** sell **fresh, small-batch olive oil** from regional producers. This is a great way to:
- Support local businesses
- Get **fresher oil** (olive oil degrades over time)
- Try **single-origin or flavored oils** (e.g., lemon, garlic, chili-infused)

**How to find:**
- Search **"farmers market near me"** on Google
- Check **LocalHarvest.org** for olive oil producers

### **5. International & Ethnic Grocery Stores**
For **authentic imported olive oil**, try:
- **Italian markets** (look for **DOP/PDO** labels like **Terra Creta, Monini, Filippo Berio**)
- **Greek markets** (Kalamata olive oil is popular)
- **Middle Eastern markets** (Lebanese, Syrian, or Turkish olive oil)
- **Spanish markets** (Picual, Arbequina, or Hojiblanca varieties)

### **6. Warehouse Clubs (Bulk Buying)**
If you use a lot of olive oil, **Costco, Sam’s Club, or BJ’s** offer good deals on large bottles:
- **Costco:** Kirkland Signature Extra Virgin Olive Oil (highly rated)
- **Sam’s Club:** Member’s Mark Extra Virgin Olive Oil

### **7. Health Food Stores**
Stores like **Sprouts, Natural Grocers, or Vitamin Shoppe** often carry **organic, cold-pressed EVOO** from smaller brands.

### **8. Subscription Services**
Some companies offer **olive oil subscriptions** for fresh deliveries:
- **Brightland** (California-based, high-quality EVOO)
- **The Olive Oil Source** ([theoliveoilsource.com](https://www.theoliveoilsource.com))
- **Olive Oil Lovers Club** ([oliveoillovers.com](https://www.oliveoillovers.com))

---

### **What to Look for When Buying Olive Oil**
✅ **Extra Virgin (EVOO)** – Highest quality, least processed
✅ **Dark glass or tin bottle** – Protects from light (which degrades oil)
✅ **Harvest date** – Fresher is better (look for **<18 months old**)
✅ **Origin** – Single-origin (e.g., **Greek, Italian, Spanish, Californian**) is better than blends
✅ **Certifications** – **DOP/PDO (EU), USDA Organic, NAOOA (North American Olive Oil Association)**
❌ **Avoid:** "Pure" or "Light" olive oil (highly refined, lower quality)

---

### **Best Olive Oil Brands by Category**
| **Category** | **Best Brands** |
|-------------|----------------|
| **Budget-Friendly** | Bertolli, Filippo Berio, Pompeian |
| **Mid-Range** | Colavita, California Olive Ranch, Lucini |
| **Premium EVOO** | Brightland, Cobram Estate, Kasandrinos, Gaea |
| **Imported (Italian)** | Terra Creta, Monini, Filippo Berio (DOP) |
| **Imported (Greek)** | Iliada, Minerva, Gaea |
| **Imported (Spanish)** | Carbonell, Borges, Picual |
| **Flavored** | Brightland (AWAKE, ALIVE), Boyajian, La Tourangelle |

---

### **Final Tips**
- **Store properly:** Keep in a **cool, dark place** (not near the stove).
- **Use within 6 months** of opening for best flavor.
- **Taste before buying** (if possible) – good EVOO should have a **peppery, fruity, or grassy** taste.

Would you like recommendations based on a specific use (cooking, drizzling, dipping, etc.)?
